sources.quote: 1.6. Stress. A satisfactory analysis of stress features has not been made. A general but incomplete statement is here given, intended as an aid to the reading of cited Zoque forms. Stress groups vary with different utterances and different speakers. In general, a stress group may be said to consist of a single word (pan man, manu he went, mapyahke?tutih they went again) or a close-knit phrase (manba minu he is going to come, manbatih minu he is just going to come). Stress is usually on the penult of the stress group, with a secondary stress on the first syllable if there are three or more syllables: ['minu] he came, [,min'ge?tu] he also came, [,minge?'tutih] he came again, [,mindapge?'tutih] you (pl.) came again, [,mapba 'minu] he is going to come, [,manbatih 'minu] he is just going to come
sources.note: Catalog rule (penult primary, initial secondary from 3 syllables: stress placement coded per word length as 10 110 1010 10010 (1 = a stressed syllable)) matches the stated pattern. Refinements stated in the work: the domain is the 'stress group' (a word or a close-knit phrase), not strictly the word; a monosyllabic word forming its own stress group is stressed; a stress group ending in a monosyllabic stem as compound member usually stresses that final stem ([kasnam'ban] ladino, [,cinuh'pan] bee, [,cinuh'tak] syrup-house, [,masan'na?] holy water); stress is 'variable within certain limits' and…

En este diccionario hay algunas otras palabras que no siguen las reglas anteriores, y llevan acento escrito (tuchtucujú' "torcaza"; siquití'n "chicharra").' sources.note: Datapoint page read: 'Datapoint Zoque (Copainalá) / Tone.. Value: No tones.. Wonderly 1951a'. I.e. Maddieson codes Copainalá Zoque as non-tonal on the basis of Wonderly's phonemic description, which lists no tonemes and treats pitch as intonation (Wonderly 1951 Zoque II p. 108: 'Further investigation of Zoque stress should be combined with an analysis of the intonational (pitch) features'; fn. 7: emphatic intonation 'consisting in low tone and strong stress on the penult, high tone and lengthening on the final syllable').
